NFL backs New Jersey's Supreme Court bid against Kalshi, while its sportsbook partners keep advertising on game day

"NFL asked US Supreme Court to take up prediction market case. So the NFL filed an amicus brief Thursday, supporting New Jersey's request I told you about in the past for Supreme Court review in its dispute with Kalshi."

"The central question is whether sports event contracts obviously fall under federal financial regulation or state gambling oversight. And curiously, NFL is stepping in on the side of the states."

"I'm going to imagine that the NFL makes a hell of a lot of money in the current iteration with gambling and sportsbooks, and that they probably want to protect the incumbency in the way that it's done, and that prediction markets make that more difficult for them. But I will reserve judgment until we see it later."

"It's funny that the NFL here is literally stepping in and saying it's about consumers. They want to remind you that gambling is dangerous, but then you can just watch the commercial from their sportsbook partner on the game. It's not that they can act like they want you to gamble responsibly, but really they just want you to gamble. As we know, the football gambling industry is much bigger than the football industry itself."

"The battle between the federal government, the states, and now even the NFL stepping up massively, and everybody's taking sides. It's pretty crazy that it seems almost inevitable now, at this point, that prediction markets are going to make it to the Supreme Court."
